title: Stamp 3: French Media Landscape
welcome_lead: Map out the French media: press, social networks, and journalism.
meta_desc: A-Level French adventure on French press, social networks, and journalism vocabulary.
final_note: Media stamp earned. You can now discuss the French press.

concepts.def: Print press, including newspapers (Le Monde, Le Figaro, Liberation) and magazines.
Social networks (Facebook, X, Instagram, TikTok); central to modern public discourse.
Journalism as a profession; freedom of press is protected by the 1881 law.
Fourth estate; the press as a check on government power.

walkthroughs.body_html: Le Monde (centre-left), Le Figaro (centre-right), and Liberation (left) are leading daily newspapers. Print circulation has declined as readers move to digital platforms.
French politicians use les reseaux sociaux extensively. Emmanuel Macron's 2017 campaign was largely powered by digital communication, including platforms like Twitter (now X).
Un journaliste = journalist. Un reportage = report. Un article de fond = feature article. Un editorial = editorial. La liberte de la presse = press freedom.

mcqs.q: How do you say 'I am using my phone right now' (emphasising the action is in progress)?
options: It means just my mother.
Je suis en train d'utiliser mon portable.
Je suis utilisant mon portable.
Je vais utiliser mon portable.

mcqs.q: How do you say 'Currently, I am using social media' in French?
options: Actually, j'utilise les réseaux sociaux.
Récemment, j'utilise les réseaux sociaux.
Actuellement, j'utilise les réseaux sociaux.
It means just my mother.

mcqs.q: What does 'mes parents' mean in French?
options: It means just my mother.
Je vais utiliser mon portable.
It always means all my relatives.
My parents (mother and father specifically) - but 'parents' can also mean relatives more broadly.
